facts.statement: Checkout's 5m error ratio is 0.329 and payment's is 0.334, both in fast burn. flagd is at 0.00036.
Among checkout's client spans, the only STATUS_CODE_ERROR dependency call is oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (about 0.085/s). Currency, cart and product-catalog calls are UNSET.
Payment's server-side Charge spans show STATUS_CODE_ERROR at about 0.094/s. Its 1m error ratio rises from 0.159 to 0.636 in step with checkout, peaking at 18:01.

Payment logs 32 warn lines in the window (17:57:29Z to 18:02:05Z), all with the message 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' at charge.js:48. There are no other error patterns.
A sampled failing trace shows the payment error propagating through checkout and frontend to a 422 at frontend-proxy.
p95 latency is flat: payment about 1.9 ms, checkout about 48 ms. The failures are hard errors, not timeouts.
Checkout has one Deployment revision (revision 1, 17:39:54Z, no change-cause). Payment also has one revision (17:39:54Z), with no restarts and no warning events.
The only enabled flag is paymentFailure at 0.5 (50%), out of 18 flags. Its change time is not recorded in the data.
Cluster warning events in the last 120 minutes are readiness-probe failures on otel-collector-agent, alertmanager and loki. None involve checkout or payment.
Checkout logs no error or warn lines. Its other dependencies show no failures in the sampled traces.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check flagd flag change history or audit logs for paymentFailure, and its targeting rules (loyalty_level). Compare the flag's on-time with the first payment error at 17:57:29Z.
hypotheses.statement: paymentFailure was switched ON at about 17:57Z and is what causes the 'Invalid token' rejections. Its 50% setting does not fully match the 32% failure rate, so targeting may be involved.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Read payment's charge.js:48 token validation path and its config/secret/ConfigMap history for changes around 17:57Z. Check whether the error reproduces for gold-tier test users.
hypotheses.statement: Payment's token validation has a bug affecting gold loyalty users, possibly triggered by a config or secret change not recorded as a Deployment revision.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check flagd logs and flag evaluation errors. Confirm checkout's errors reproduce with payment bypassed. Flagd error ratio is 0.00036, so this is unlikely.
hypotheses.statement: A flagd-side or shared-dependency issue is affecting both checkout and payment (checkout's flags come from flagd).

inferences.statement: Payment is the origin and checkout is a symptom. The error is raised in payment's Charge handler and propagates up through checkout to the frontend, and the error timing matches.
Failure rates match: 100 'Charge request received' vs 68 'Transaction complete' is about 32% failing, consistent with checkout's ~26.6% ratio.
A recent rollout is unlikely to be the cause, since neither service changed in the 20 minutes before the alert. The more likely trigger is a flag or runtime state change in payment.

root_causes.cause: Payment's Charge handler rejects about a third of charges with an 'Invalid token' error scoped to gold loyalty users. Checkout surfaces this through PaymentService/Charge. The likely trigger is the paymentFailure flag (ON at 50%), though this is not confirmed.
A payment-side code or config change in token/loyalty validation, not visible in revision history (payment has only revision 1 from 17:39:54Z). This is less likely than the flag and is unverified.

diagnosis.summary: checkout's ~26.6% error ratio is caused by payment. Payment's Charge calls fail with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' (about 32% of charges, concentrated on gold users), starting about 17:57-17:58Z. Checkout's only failing dependency call is PaymentService/Charge, and latency is flat, so these are hard errors. No rollout happened on either service. The only enabled flag is paymentFailure at 50%, which is the most likely trigger, but its on-time is not in the data.

facts.statement: Feature flag paymentFailure is ON with a 50% variant and is the only one of 18 flags on.
Payment and checkout each have a single Deployment revision created at 17:39:54Z with no change-cause, and no warnings, restarts or OOM kills appear in events.

payment's Charge spans fail with exception 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' at charge.js:48, and erroring spans appear in 19-20 of 20 sampled error traces.
payment logs 27 warn-level lines in 15 minutes, all with the same message. It has zero ERROR-level lines, so error-level alerting would miss these failures.
payment's server Charge spans error at about 0.084/s and its internal charge span at about 0.098/s. The share of erroring requests is 0.27-0.55 in 1m windows from 17:58 to 18:01.
payment's dependency client spans (flagd, dns, tcp) show no errors, and its p95 latency is flat at about 1.9 ms.
checkout's client Charge error rate to payment matches payment's server error rate, and checkout's PlaceOrder errors carry the same payment message.
payment and checkout error ratios rose together from about 0.038 at 17:58 to about 0.33 at 18:01, so resolution does not show which started first.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the flagd change history or flag-config git log for paymentFailure's modification time and author.
hypotheses.statement: paymentFailure was switched on shortly before 18:00Z, which would make it the trigger.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Split payment Charge spans and logs by demo.user_context.loyalty_level and compare error rates per tier.
hypotheses.statement: Failures are concentrated in gold-tier users, which would explain the ~28% rate versus 50% flag setting.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Set paymentFailure to off in flagd in the lab, then watch service:sli_error_ratio:rate5m for payment and checkout over 5-10 minutes.
hypotheses.statement: Turning paymentFailure off restores payment's error ratio to baseline and clears the checkout and frontend errors.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Read payment charge.js around line 48 and test a gold-tier charge with the flag off.
hypotheses.statement: Some payment failures may be real rather than injected, if the token validation logic is wrong for gold users.

inferences.statement: payment is the origin and checkout's failures are inherited from it. checkout shows no change and no errors of its own beyond its Charge calls.

The failure is an intentional fault in payment's Charge handler, most likely the paymentFailure flag. The 50% setting versus about 28% observed suggests only part of charge traffic hits the faulty path, such as a subset of users.

root_causes.cause: payment's Charge path fails a share of requests with an injected-looking 'Invalid token' error, most likely driven by the flagd paymentFailure flag being ON at 50%. No rollout, restart or dependency fault explains it. The flag switch-on time is not confirmed.
a payment-side token validation defect scoped to loyalty_level=gold users, independent of the flag. Weak: the message names the tier but no per-tier split was shown.

diagnosis.summary: payment is the origin of the ErrorBudgetBurn. Its Charge handler throws 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' for roughly 28% of requests (about 44% in a partial log sample). Those errors propagate to checkout (gRPC 13) and frontend/frontend-proxy (HTTP 422), so checkout is a downstream victim. Payment and checkout were not redeployed, and the only active change signal is feature flag paymentFailure at 50%. The switch-on time is unverified. Mitigation: confirm and disable paymentFailure in flagd, then recheck payment's error ratio.
